ceo_letter.title: CEO
promises: Continuing sales and marketing efforts at current level for port terminals
Liquidation of Hove Brazil to be completed by end of 2025
Liquidation costs to be kept within DKK 0.3 million provision
Developing new sales and distribution strategy for South American market

themes.theme: Wind turbine segment pumps and grease

challenges.mitigation: Better-than-expected sales and order intake more than offset the adverse effect

challenges.challenge: Seasonal fluctuations from large customer in Turkey
No new port terminal contracts in Q3

honesty_signals: Transparency about gross margin decline from 38.3% to 34.6% with specific reason (higher private label share)
Acknowledgement of not winning new port terminal contracts in Q3
Detailed disclosure of exchange rate impact (11% decline)
Specific provision disclosure for Brazil liquidation costs (DKK 0.3 million)
Admission of seasonal fluctuations affecting Turkey performance
key_quotes: The better-than-expected sales and order intake more than offset the adverse effect from a decline in the USD/DKK exchange rate of 11%.
EBITDA, EBIT and net profit for Q1-Q3 2025 exceed the corresponding figures for the whole of 2024.
The EBITDA margin improved from 10.9% in the first nine months of 2024 to 12.4% in 2025.
Hove's solvency ratio was 74% at the end of Q3, and Hove thus maintains its strong capital structure and low financial risk.

key_narratives: Organic revenue growth driven by wind turbine segment demand
Successful international expansion with cash-generating subsidiaries
Operational efficiency improving despite margin compression
Strategic restructuring in South America (Brazil liquidation)
Strong balance sheet supporting growth initiatives
mda_analysis.management_interpretation: Management interprets Q3 results as demonstrating strong operational momentum and successful execution of growth strategy. Despite margin pressure from product mix shift (more private label), significant improvements in EBITDA margin (from 10.9% to 12.4%) and absolute EBITDA (+45%) indicate effective cost management. Management views the guidance upgrade as validation of better-than-expected performance, with results already exceeding full-year 2024 figures for key metrics. International subsidiaries are performing well despite external challenges.

guidance.commentary: Management raised guidance significantly on both revenue and EBITDA, indicating high confidence in momentum. Q1-Q3 EBITDA of DKK 20.6M is already at the low end of new full-year guidance, with strong Q4 typically expected. Revenue of DKK 165.3M through Q3 suggests DKK 35-45M needed in Q4 to meet guidance, which is achievable given Q3's DKK 57.0M performance.

executive_summary: Hove delivered strong Q3 2025 results with 28% revenue growth to DKK 57.0M and 45% EBITDA growth to DKK 20.6M YTD, driven by wind turbine segment performance and international expansion. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue (DKK 200-210M) and EBITDA (DKK 21-24M), with Q1-Q3 results already exceeding full-year 2024 figures, despite margin pressure from higher private label mix and currency headwinds.
key_highlights: Revenue: DKK 57.0M in Q3 (+28% YoY), DKK 165.3M YTD (+27%)
EBITDA: DKK 7.4M in Q3 (+12%), DKK 20.6M YTD (+45%) with margin improving from 10.9% to 12.4%
Guidance raised significantly: Revenue to DKK 200-210M (from 180-200M), EBITDA to DKK 21-24M (from 15-20M)
Strong balance sheet with 74% solvency ratio, cash position grew from DKK 4.4M to DKK 7.6M
US and India subsidiaries performing well and cash flow positive despite external challenges
Q1-Q3 EBITDA, EBIT, and net profit already exceed full-year 2024 figures
Free cash flow of DKK 3.2M despite paying DKK 3.5M dividend
